description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 7 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This model is my very first attempt of doing a Tardis control room with a TARDIS Console, I know there are far better models than this, I used what was available to me and what I was able to do to create the console controls
I do not know how to make domed shapes or do wires, so I used different shapes and try to be consistent with the pattern layout, only two panels are slightly different, but that is because I wanted it to be that way.    Other than this, I was inventive putting roundals into the base of the TARDIS Console, which I do not think that has been done before, certainly not in Doctor Who console History.
I experimented with having a rod inside the Time Rotor, I made it a hexagon shaped one, as I felt that added a better extra dimension than a cylinder rod, the whole control room and console follows a pattern, of circles and hexagons, the roundals are randomly placed and of random sizes.
They are meant to be that way, adding what I feel that cookie style befitting of any Doctor, the console is almost like the Peter Davison/Colin Baker/Sylvester McCoy's TARDIS Console, I even put roundals on the door frame of the Interior door.  I wanted to have a metalic look to the console, some of what I call touch plates, also nob controls are meant to be sort of organic in nature.

description_text: The inspiration for this model came from a resin aquarium castle that has openings for the fish to swim thru.  Always looking for subject matter. Walking tour: Ground level- Multi-purpose room with a wood stove connection, right is a hobby room, bar, bath, and round tower room.  Left rear is the main stairs.  Rite down a hall, past a mechanical room and Elevator is the Theatre.  Main floor - large Living Room with Fireplace, Main stairs, 1/4 circle Dining Room with Fireplace, eat-in Kitchen with a large circular pantry.  Left down the hall with Elevator and Closet is the Office with a Bath and Closet.  Bedroom level - 2 Bedrooms, Bath and Laundry.  Rite goes to Terrace and Tower Room. Left down the hall, past Elevator is another Terrace and Tower Room.  Attic level- Master Suite with Bath and Closet.  Rite to the Closet and Elevator.  It was fun putting an interior into this model.  After all, it is what it is.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This 1890 house with a Mansard roof is almost the same as the floor plan.  Had this in my office for a couple of months just wondering what exterior I would put on it.  Well, here it is.  Changes: 1st floor - updated the kitchen, elimated door betweer front Parlor and Living Room.  Parlor could be used as an Office.  Rather strange place for the 1st floor toilet.  It is in the back of the coat closet, behind the coats!  Butler's pantry remains under the stair landing.  Upstairs changed the front left Bedroom into 2 Baths and a Closet and made the old Bathroom into the Laundry.  Finally, tacked a 2-car Garage onto the rear.  Interior stairs to the cellar is replace by the trap door in the Garage.  Pocket doors downstairs are closed via layers.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This is a model of a Pola kit that came in a beat up box.  After haggeling with the owner of the hobby shop where I bought it, I got 50% of retail.  This is a shell, you can finish the interior however you want to. There is a truck loading dock on one side, and a train door on the other, at least I think that is what it is.  To me, this looks like two separate buildings joined together.  There is a sign board over the office door, the other half is the manufactureing area with a large exhaust pipe on the roof.  The purpose of the other strucure on the roof is unknown.  Finally there is an old boiler room on the side with a large propane tank in the covered area.  Model came out OK.  It is what it is. At least I had leftover parts for the scrap box!  Bob   update: K. Boom Fireworks Ltd. ?

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 These are the walls for the Victorian House upper attic.  Instructions:  Save to a folder, open the High-Victorian house, then import these wall into the house.  Have already done it - it works.  It actually went where it was supposed to!  Component axis is at the front left corner on the floor template- opposite from view.  It should drop right in. Turn off layers above attic and Shadows first, though.  Neat trick: create' attic walls' layer and keep this on that layer.  This way you can stand in the attic and turn off and on the walls to compare the space allocation.  Deleted wall ends, floor, and tops to eliminate z-fighting.  You can edit component to add doors, plumbing, etc.  Door is in component listing.  Used Wheat for the wall colour- I painted the attic to match.  I use Sketchup for Dummies to help me.  Very useful.  Bob Update:  installed these walls into the attic - see Victorain House with attic- for those people who may not want to do this.  Axis is off by 1/16 inch.  Move it forward 1/16" or so.  Made a component out of the floor, so it should have fit.  Just in the wrong place.  Oops!

This makes Commerce Place the 7th tallest building complex in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. It is situated on the corners of King Street East and James Street North. It is the site where the Bank of Hamilton was established in 1872. in 1905 the Bank was doing so well it expanded its head office, adding on an additional 8 stories. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The Confederation Building is a gothic revival office building in Ottawa, Canada. Located just west of the Parliament Buildings at Bank and Wellington Streets, it is generally considered part of Parliament Hill. Originally the land where the Confederation Building, and also the Supreme Court of Canada, now stand had contained homes and businesses. These were expropriated by the government to allow for the construction of new federal buildings. The new building was designed by Clarence Burritt. Work on the Confederation Building began when the cornerstone was laid by the Governor General on July 1, 1927 as part of the celebrations of Canada's Diamond Jubilee and it opened during 1931. It originally housed workers in a number of departments, with the Department of Agriculture being the largest tenant. Today it is home both to civil servants and to a number of MPs and ministers. As part of the ongoing work on Parliament Hill there are currently discussions to fill the space between the Confederation Building and the smaller Justice Building to create more office space.

Combining Art-Deco and Gothic-Revival elements, the building incorporated glass from Belgium, window frames from England, and interior decoration in marble, tile, and murals painted by church decorators of events related to building of the skyscraper. In true Gotham-style, there were, atop the roof, rotating searchlights that revolved every 30 seconds. The building remained a thriving commercial office development until the 1970's, when the downtown economy began to wane. During the next decade the skyscraper was sold and resold several times for a variety of projects, but all fell through. Fortunately, it was designated as being of heritage interest in 1984.

description_text: The Palacio de Congresos of Badajoz is opened in 2006 and built inside the bastion of San Roque, the seventeenth century building. The palace is the work of architects José Selgas and Lucía Cano Laso, and was built by the Junta de Extremadura. The building was selected for the exhibition On Site: New Architecture in Spain MOMA, along with other 52 buildings featuring the most representative of the new Spanish architecture of the last 30 years. Since its construction it has become a true symbol of the vanguard of Extremadura. The palace is erected on the site where the old bullring, known as the scene of one of the largest massacres occurred during the Spanish Civil War was located.

SummaryDo you want a plant at your desk but are housed in a cubicle farm without any hope of UV light?  Or are you one of those people who can kill un-killable plants? Then grow your own Modular Customizable Desk Plant!  It will always be in bloom (if you want it to be), it will always be green (if you want it to be), and it never ever ever wants water or sunshine.  
Just be sure to put it in some soil or rocks or the poor thing might grow so big it tips over!
InstructionsRequires Printing with Support  
It's easy:
1) Print out the pieces you want your plant to possess
2) Snap everything together
3) Don't forget to put it into a pot with soil!  
The awesome Rose is courtesy of ProCoPrint3D  
If you have your own ends you wish to attach to your plant, use the Connection Pin extra or just modify the Solidworks files available in the SW_Parts.zip

This is the second tallest building in the city, standing at 15 civilian floors but with two plant floors above, making it 17 stories high. A building completed/opened in 1968, it does have stories to tell for it changed hands several times. It was originally Paulwall National Bank but it went bankrupt a bout 15 years ago, then Wells Fargo bought the building a decade ago. Wells Fargo bank lives on the first couple of stories, then the upper floors are rented to tenants to house offices and general business. There is an accounting office up there, a printing office, publishing office, law firm, and even a credit union. A few floors remain empty as they await tenants. So nothing unlike a regular office building in any downtown setting. In terms of banking, Paulwall has a good multitude of different banks all around the city. This just happens to be the largest of them all. I hope you enjoy this highrise office building and please rate :)

description_text:
This is my BGE-Playground, which I had created in Blender from 17.11.2013 to 10.12.2013 for fun. http://wp.me/P3dmoi-1na
Navigation Mesh Test EXTREME https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Okd7ihFGiQ&amp
Fun with Suspend and Restore Dynamics https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nXgbuVFwenM
BGE Test Building 1.0 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HfyxBEOuczc&amp
Building Update (just added some old 3d Models) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TWQXLN8SrZk
Building Update (controllable ceiling lights and doors) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9S5UMzIQW_s
Just another futuristic building I am working on https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kF9xFSCOj_4
All the objects you find in this blendfile are 100% game ready with collision-boxes and grouped-objects etc. The game-objects are located in the Objects-Scene and are linked to the other scenes. There are three main scenes Low, Medium, High and Menu. Unfortunately the Menu-scene works randomly, so blender crashes about 90% when I try this scene, I guess this is some kid of Blender bug. Low-Secne - No interior and exterior-objects, just doors and light Medium-Secne - All interior and exterior-objects High-Secne - All interior and exterior-objects + sun shadow (4K) This Blendfile starts in the Low-Scene.
Basic control:

  - W- Key - move forward

  -  S- Key - move back

  -  A- Key - move to the left

  -  D- Key - move to the right

  -  F- Key - jump

  -  Left Mouse Button - activate the lights

  -  E- Key - open Doors

  -  Left-Shift- Key - zoom in and out

  -  Space- Key - hold to run

Object controls:

  - Right Mouse Button -throw the green navigation spheres which interact with the navigation mesh and tries to follow the PlayerBox-Object

  -  E- Key - throw the red navigation spheres which do not interact with the navigation mesh and tries to follow the PlayerBox-Object

  -  T- Key - throw the blue spheres which flee from the PlayerBox-Object

  -  Z- Key - throw the metallic spheres which lose their dynamics on 3 meters distance to the PlayerBox-Object

  -  G- Key - throw a simple sphere without special properties

  -  H- Key - throw the soft body object number 1, a softbody plane

  -  J- Key - throw the soft body object number 2, a softbody cube

  -  B- Key - throw a destructible box

  -  Q- Key - restores the dynamics of all the objects which have suspended their dynamics

Daylight control:
  -  you can control the daylight/daytime by pressing the + and - key right to the Numpad.
2D -filter control:
  -  you can activate and deactivate the standard 2D-filter by pressing 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,0- key on the Numpad
Feel free to:
test your computer-performance with it :) make some Videos about it (just would like to see some tests on a high-end pc ^^ ) use some of those objects for your game, as long as it is not commercially give me criticism, suggestions or ideas for version 2.0 Have fun while exploring and hope you like it : )

description_text:
This model was created in Cinema4d r20 and is made to render with arnold 5. The only texture that is included is a specular roughness map for the metal (it is darker instead of lighter as a specular map would be). If you are going to use this in another program besides cinema4d and arnold render, you will have to recreate the semi-transparent texture of the light bulb glass. The glass is made by adding transmission in arnold renderer (i.e. transparency or refraction) to the bulb but not too much. In vray you may need to reduce the refraction glossiness to remake a similar effect.
The light includes 3 arnold lights within the model, one near the top for the light on the ceiling, one in the middle to illuminate the inside of the bulb and one below the bulb to shine light on the ground. Light nodes are included in the fbx file however they will most likely not function the same by default when you open them in another program.
Turning on and off the light: There is an on group and an off group in the light model. Simply make one visible and make another one not visible and it will function correctly and turn off the lights once you disable the on group and visa versa.
An .fbx is included in the .rar file for use in all applications
Lighting scene is included as light_01Presentation.c4d

This model was created in Cinema4d r20 and is made to render with arnold 5. Diffuse and specular map are included however the specular map is not hooked up or used in the render (included as optional). An .fbx is included in the .rar file for use in other applications however you will have to recreate the semi transparent glass texture for the bulb. The glass is made by adding transmission in arnold renderer (i.e. transparency or refraction) to the bulb but not too much. In vray you may need to reduce the refraction glossiness to remake a similar effect so you can see the light through the glass (ie, it has a "hot spot).
The light includes 3 arnold lights within the model: one in the middle to illuminate the inside of the bulb, one below the bulb to shine light on the ground, and another below the bulb to shine light up on the ceiling and to cast a minor shadow around the base of the model. Light nodes are included in the fbx file however they will most likely not function the same by default when you open them in another program.
Turning on and off the light: There is an on group and an off group in the light model. Simply make one visible and make another one not visible and it will function correctly and turn off the lights once you disable the on group and visa versa.
An .fbx is included in the .rar file for use in all applications
Lighting scene is included as light_02Presentation.c4d

description_text:
Vivianna Corporate Park is a master-planned community located in Vivianna, North Carolina, an affluent suburb south of Charlotte. The 102-acre office park features over 2.4 million square feet of Class A office space and includes the headquarters of many Fortune 500 companies and businesses. There are also many parks and greenspaces within the campus that offer recreational events and educational opportunities to Vivianna residents.
Lake Vivianna Park
Lake Vivianna Park is a 21-acre park located on the southern corner of Vivianna Corporate Park. The park surrounds the 12-acre Lake Vivianna, which has a shape of the letter V. The lake features the Lake Vivianna Fountains, a group of four floating fountains that can rise up to 70 feet high. At night, the fountains illuminate in bright, beautiful colors. The park also features the Vivianna Monuments, two 40-foot monuments located on each side of the park. The monuments represent the advancements of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).
Vivianna Nature Park
Vivianna Nature Park is a 27-acre nature park located on the northern corner of Vivianna Corporate Park. The park contains a 4-acre botanical garden on its north side and a 16-acre pine forest on its south side. The 2-acre Berkeley Pond is also located within the forest and provides great views of Vivianna’s skyline. The nature park provides educational opportunities for students and children to learn more about wildlife and the natural environment.
Everston Park
Everston Park is a 6-acre park located on the eastern corner of Vivianna Corporate Park. The park is popular for special events, festivals, and even weddings!
Macklin Park
Macklin Park is a 6-acre park located on the western corner of Vivianna Corporate Park. Just like Everston Park, this park is popular for special events, festivals, and even weddings!
Vivianna Corporate Park is based off of Ballantyne Corporate Park in Ballantyne, an affluent neighborhood in Charlotte. Feel free to use this model for any of your projects! Just make sure you give me credit!

Robert Barnby is a contemporary furniture designer with a workshop based just outside the picturesque town of Hay-on-Wye in the shadow of The Black Mountains.

description_text:
Shelf - PBR, Low poly - game ready.
Made in Blender, textured in Substance Painter and Rendered in Marmoset Toolbag 3
Contains: 1 Shelf -> 160_verts, 114_faces, 228_tris
Texture Workflow: Metallic 
Texture Sets: Standard, Unity, UE4 
Texture Size: 4k, PNG (Textures can always be scaled down, in any software if needed) 
[For texture setup read my short tutorial at the end of this description.]
Formats: FBX, OBJ, COLLAD[DAE], BLENDER[ORIGINAL]
Real world size: 58x202x165cm System units: centimeters
NOTE: I only provide you with Unity and Unreal Engine Textures and Not project example. You have to Drag in, Textures and file formats into your project yourself. 
___________UE4 Textures Setup_______
Import Base color, Normal map and Roughness-AO-Mettalic (all baked into one map) Double click Roughness-AO-Metallic and disable sRGB.
Create Material: Drag these 3 maps into it. Base color and normal map connect to their inputs. [Some of my assets don't have a normal map, so proceed without it]
Set Roughness-AO-Metallic node to linear color (Only works if you turned off sRGB before)
Connect RED channel to AO GREEN to Roughness BLUE to Metallic
That's it.
___________Unity Note_____________ To change to Linear Color Space :
I went to Edit>Project Settings>Player>Other Settings>ColorSpace and set it to Linear.

NOTE: I only provide you with Unity and Unreal Engine Textures and Not project examples. You have to Drag in, Textures and file formats into your project yourself.
NOTE: Screenshots that are taken in unity and UE4 are in default projects, no lighting or anything has been altered. Depending on your project's settings results may be different or even better.
UE4 Textures Setup
Import Base color, Normal map and Roughness-AO-Mettalic (all baked into one map) Double click Roughness-AO-Metallic and disable sRGB.
Create Material: Drag these 3 maps into it. Base color and normal map connect to their inputs. [Some of my assets don't have a normal map, so proceed without it]
Set Roughness-AO-Metallic node to linear color (Only works if you turned off sRGB before)
Connect RED channel to AO GREEN to Roughness BLUE to Metallic
That's it.
Unity Note__
To change to Linear Color Space:
I went to Edit>Project Settings>Player>Other Settings>ColorSpace and set it to Linear.

Las primeras sillas Søborg con marco de madera se lanzaron en 1950, y en 1952 la colección creció con versiones con marcos de metal. Las sillas son excelentes ejemplos del funcionalismo fresco e intemporal de Mogensen que se adapta fácilmente a cualquier entorno, desde espacios residenciales hasta restaurantes y otras áreas públicas. Las sillas Søborg se fabrican en Dinamarca.

description_text:
Wine shelf - Full parametric Revit Family
-If you want to have a fully parametric wine shelf, you can try this Revit Family.
-I've created everything to be fully adjustable and it's also absolutely easy and fast to change every parameter in Revit Family properties, so it will fit everywhere according your ideas.
-Things you are able to change, you can see in jpgs, like: Height, Width, Depth, all Materials and more. In Revit Family properties, you can change every input except for inputs from Data field, where usually all formulas are listed. So if you want change something from Data, be careful model maybe won't work properly.

  - Included also:  .fbx .dwg .obj file, which contain one piece, only in Revit Family is possible to make different types

  - All my parametric Revit Families are made from scratch with maximum quality and precision. In the end, you should be able to use it for many similar different projects. If you may know, Revit Family is a sub-program for Revit. You can create models in more complex and different shapes as usual in Revit, and if you put the right parameters for it, you can update this kind of family in more different shapes and sizes, if you have parameters set right. In my all Revit Families on this website, i'm always trying to create and add parameters for main dimensions such as width, height, depth and more and always changeable materials, if you want to put different textures.

Thank you for your time and i hope you'll like it. :)

Do you need space to store your books and other office supplies? Look no more, the ultimate solution is here! With these shelves/cabinets/storages/ whatever you want to call them, you can store even the smallest things in your office and never lose them again!

The model includes the following 2k textures:

  - Albedo

  - Normal Map

  - Packed PBR (Roughness, Metalness, Ambient Occlusion)

The packaged PBR texture has the following textures assigned on RGB channels:

  - Red = Ambient Occlusion

  - Green = Roughness

  - Blue = Metalness

If you have any questions regarding the 3D models, please do not hesitate to send me a message :)

description_text: The St. Paul Building was a 315ft (96m) tall skyscraper in New York City. Located at the intersection of Broadway and Ann St just across the street from St. Paul's Chapel, the building was a unique pioneer in New York's race to build towards the sky. The slender highrise was designed in a Beaux Arts style by prominent architect George B. Post. The building was completed in 1898 and demolished 60 years later in 1958 to make way for the Western Electric Building, a modernist office building. However, a small piece of the building still survives to this day. Karl Bitter's sculpture depicting 3 men holding up part of the building that once adorned the entrance to the St. Paul Building has been preserved and put on display in Holliday Park in Indianapolis.

description_text:
Model precisely based on the Altec Lansing ACS90, an iconic 90s looking set of speakers.
_
KEY ASPECTS
DETAIL. The model is optimized with high-res normals, and enough texel density (even 220ppu along all the UVs) and PBR detailed textures for each element to work individually on close-ups, without being a dense high-poly model.
VERSATILITY. Comes with 5 texture sets that range along basic brand new condition, yellowed plastic, different type of dirt (including full corporeal dirt as the most worn state), and an unique childist style, using crayon and markers. 
EASE OF USE. All of the settings can be easily configurable by just sliding independent attributes on a couple of controls. At the same time, every element of the shaders is well grouped and named for individual in-hypershade tweaks if wanted. 
_
TECHNICAL ELEMENTS

  - Textures are PBR; worked as UDIMs, with individual textures no bigger than 4K, and ranging down to 1k when most fitted. There are no “redundant” textures, as each one of them is used in more than once in the shading options workflow

  - Model is real size, the measures are 16.8 x 11.16 x 8.5cm for each speaker.

  - No nSided faces, no triangles. 55308 faces/55979 verts

  - No object is rigged and each is individually selectable.

Included elements:

  - Maya scene

  - UDIM textures

  - .fbx, .obj, . (individual references of each style and speaker) files

  - Sample renders (images and video)

  - Free license HDRiHeaven.com light texture

  - Thorough walktrhough the scene remaks as .txt file

_
OPTIONS DEPICTON
The following elements can be edit directly from viewport controls:
Choosing the shader:
  - Shader: Base, Used, Worn, Devil sis, Full worn
Moving knobs::

  - Volume knob: Translate X:  -0.5, 0.5 as min/max

  - Treble knob: Translate X:  -0.5, 0.5 as min/max

Light control:

  - Light: Off, on, (linked to ON OFF controller)

  - On Off:  (moves the button and turns on the light)

Hope you find it of use, and of course any questions are welcomed.
Till next time, Manuel.
_

This laptop model is available for use for any application. You can edit it or keep it the same, the choice is yours. I would recommend downloading the zip version as it has the readme and keyboard textures folder included. Blend file contains some basic procedural materials. The UV map of the monitor screen may be flipped horizontally on some files so for editing the contents of the screen, you may need to scale your UV map by -1 on the X axis. 
On the left side there are three generic looking ports. Interior of the ports are not modelled.
The back of the monitor also has a square UV unwrap for applying a logo. I'm not very good at UV unwrapping so I apologise if it is a bit messy.
Laptop screen has origin point correctly positioned so it is easily opened or closed.
Thank you for having a look at my model! Enjoy your day.
